item.title: Chicken Nanban — Guide
item.description: Chicken nanban (chikin nanban) is Miyazaki’s most famous home-grown dish and a nationwide favourite that originated in the city of Nobeoka. Pieces of chicken — usually thigh — are battered and deep-fried until golden and crisp, then dipped while still hot into a sweet-and-sour ‘nanban’ vinegar sauce (soy, vinegar and sugar), which soaks in to give a wonderful sweet-tangy flavour. The dish is then generously topped with a thick, creamy tartar sauce made with mayonnaise, chopped boiled egg, onion and pickles.

item.title: Ghibli Museum — Guide
item.description: The Ghibli Museum in Mitaka, western Tokyo, is a magical, whimsical museum dedicated to the works of Studio Ghibli, the legendary animation studio behind films like My Neighbour Totoro, Spirited Away and Princess Mononoke. Designed under the direction of Hayao Miyazaki himself, the museum is a playful, storybook-like building full of winding staircases, stained glass, hidden nooks and surprises, deliberately laid out to be explored freely rather than in a set route.

item.title: Hiyajiru: Miyazaki's Cold Soup — Guide
item.description: Hiyajiru (‘cold soup’) is Miyazaki’s traditional summer comfort food, a refreshing and nutritious dish perfectly suited to the prefecture’s hot, humid climate. It’s made from a chilled broth of miso blended with grilled and ground fish (often flying fish or aji), toasted sesame and dashi, seasoned and thinned with cold water into a savoury, nutty, umami-rich soup. This is then poured over a bowl of rice and topped with cool ingredients like sliced cucumber, shiso leaf, myoga ginger and tofu.

item.title: Miyazaki Mango — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki’s warm, sunny climate makes it Japan’s leading producer of premium mangoes, and its top-grade fruit is a byword for luxury. The most famous are the ‘Taiyō no Tamago’ (‘Eggs of the Sun’) — flawless, jewel-like mangoes that must meet strict standards for size, sugar content and a deep, even red colour to earn the brand name. Left to ripen fully on the tree until they naturally drop into protective nets, they are picked at peak perfection, giving an intensely sweet, richly fragrant, silky-smooth flesh with almost no fibre.
